title: Scratch-Word Comparison Loop
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, and $q$ a rational number. For every natural number $w$ and register state $\sigma$, suppose the scratch register equals $w$, every register is at most $B$, and the input pointer plus twice the length of the binary expansion of the scratch value plus two is at most $B$. If the binary expansion of the scratch value is doubled at the input pointer, then the configuration at the comparison-exit state, with the pointer advanced by that amount and the scratch register cleared, has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If that doubled-word pattern does not occur, suppose that for every pointer and scratch-register value at most $B$, the configuration at the fallback state with those values has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. Then the comparison-loop configuration with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.

replaced:
Fix a bit-string input $x$, a register bound $B$, and a rational number $q$. For every
natural number $w$ and register state $\sigma$, suppose the scratch register equals $w$,
every register is at most $B$, and the input pointer plus twice the length of the binary
expansion of $w$, plus two, is at most $B$. If the input has the required doubled-word
pattern at the pointer, then the comparison-exit configuration—with pointer advanced by
that amount and the scratch register cleared—has probabilistic semantics with acceptance
probability $q$. If it does not have that pattern, suppose every configuration at the
fallback state, for all pointer and scratch-register values at most $B$, has
probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. Then the comparison-loop
configuration with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance
probability $q$.
